standard_prerequisites.name: Regular N1i derivations and fresh eigenvariables
standard_prerequisites.statement: The original natural-deduction rules, assumption-discharge convention, regularity definition and author renaming/substitution arguments are explicitly retained as context. N1i excludes the classical absurdity rule. No new hypothesis or proof case is inserted.

core_obligations: Retain the actual segment/rank/length definitions and core permutation and reduction conversions, not the short induction alone
Retain the topmost/rightmost restrictions that control copied cuts and the original eigenvariable regularity framework
Count only the author N1i weak-normalization theorem; subsequent strong-normalization remark and N2i transfer statement are uncounted context
proof_roadmap: 第 1 步：By induction on the cut rank and length of~\delta. The induction hypothesis is that any proof which either has lower cut rank, or the same cut rank but lower cut length, normalizes.

第 2 步：If the cut length is~0, there are no cuts, \delta is already normal. So assume that cut rank and cut length of~\delta are~> 0. Pick a topmost, rightmost maximal cut segment. If the cut segment has length >1, apply a permutation conversion.
items.difficulty_reason: H2: this is not a direct syntax induction. The author defines maximal cut segments, orders derivations by cut rank and total maximal cut length, and controls duplication by selecting topmost/rightmost maximal cuts. Permutation conversions shorten long segments while preserving eigenvariable conditions; reduction conversions control newly generated cuts by their lower formula rank. The core conversion arguments and diagrams are retained together with the short main induction under one parent. Author routine rule-pair exercises remain exercises; they are not assistant-solved or separate questions.

preamble_spans.label: Open Logic Project layer-3 adapter preamble: the project's own formulas/tokenize/selective style layer and its own open-logic-config.sty, so the author's shorthand, rule names, text tokens and tag conditionals are the author's own

editorial_notes: All mathematical statement and proof text is reproduced verbatim from the Open Logic Project, unit proof-theory, file normalization-thm.tex, fixed at commit 1e960beff9ed7835bf3e3f1335e21af3439cd107. Only the packaging (the adapter preamble and the standalone wrapper) is this module's.
Numbering inside this standalone excerpt is editorial, not the Open Logic Project print numbering.

The adapter preamble loads the project's OWN style layer verbatim (sty/open-logic-formulas.sty, sty/open-logic-tokenize.sty, sty/open-logic-selective.sty and open-logic-config.sty, including its tag truth assignment), so the author's !! text-token shorthand, !A math metavariables, rule names (Intro, Elim, FalseInt) and the tag conditionals resolve exactly as in the book. Three substitutions are forced by the pinned toolchain and are recorded: isomath.sty is absent so \mathsfit is \mathsf; xpunctuate.sty is absent and unused so its RequirePackage is dropped; thmtools/ntheorem are absent so the environments are amsthm with the project's family numbering. The proof trees are the project's own bussproofs-extra.

The H2 judgement and its reason were made in this module by reading the author's own statement and complete proof at the pinned line span. Original candidate key: proof-theory/normalization|normalization-thm.tex|thm:normalization.

Reference labels in the proof resolve to navigation pointers to the original author source; these pointers do not reproduce proofs of the prerequisites. The author's own ollabel is kept unprefixed (not part:chapter:section) so those pointers resolve; the label text itself is the author's own argument.
